Durchlauchtigster Fürst

Gnädigster Herr!

Wann ich auf irgend einer Art die 25000 rt, ohne das große Geschäfte zu machen, erhalten können, so hätte ich solches längst mit den glühendesten Eyfer bewürkt.

Nehme aber das wenigere so kostet es und die Hände sind mir gebunden, weil ich die schweren Papiere bey den Kleinen Anlehn, so gut als bey den großen verpfänden muß. Noch habe ich keine erste Versiche rung war ich die Capitalien erhalten ſoll. Mann findet die Pappiere gut, und die Sicherheit sufficient aber man zögert, Gott weis warum.

Ich thue gewis alles was Menschliche Kräfte vermög und Ruhe noch Raste nicht, wen an Ziel aller Wünsche zu gelangen. Nur erzwingen läst sich hier nichts Schon 2 mahl glaubten wir das Geld gewis zu haben aber ein böser Mensch hat es hintertrieben, wie ich denke

ist es der junge Eyſenhardt — der will an Ewr Durchlaucht auch 18000 rt zu fordern haben, für diese will ihm der Hoft Rath Meyer die 20000 rt angeben und die Schuld annehmen — ich habe dies vor der Hand abgewiesen — weil der Prozeß wegen den Janvelen noch nicht entschieden ist und weil, die 9000 rthl auf Szetlewek eingetragen daher er mit den Zinsen zufrieden sein muß die ich ihm selbst zu zahlen eine Versicherung gegeben habe. Eben so werde ich mit der Ziemeckischen Sache machen Von Bernhardis Benehmen schweige ich — den er wolte mich ärger als der gröste Wucherer in Staate behandeln und sezte mich durch eine 11 tägige Verzögerung in die allergrößte Verlegenheit — Gott lob ich habe die Sache glücklich als ich es denken konte beendiget und laße den Bauer laufen.

Solte die Schlabrendorffen unartig sein, so ist hier für alles gesorgt, und sie allen würde ein thörigtes Benehmen zu bereuen haben.

translation.en:
156

Most Serene Prince,

Most gracious Lord!

If I had been able in any way whatever to obtain the 25000 Rthl without making the great transaction, I should long since have brought it about with the most glowing zeal.

But if I take the lesser sum, it costs, and my hands are tied, because I must pledge the heavy papers for the small loans just as much as for the large ones. As yet I have no first assurance [uncertain: when] I am to receive the capitals. The papers are found good and the security sufficient, but there is delay, God knows why.

I am certainly doing everything of which human powers are capable, and neither rest nor repose, [uncertain: in order] to reach the goal of all wishes. Only here nothing can be forced. Twice already we believed we had the money for certain, but an evil man has thwarted it; as I think,

it is young Eysenhardt — who claims to have 18000 Rthl to demand of Your Serene Highness as well; for these the Court Councillor Meyer will offer him the 20000 Rthl and take over the debt — I have declined this for the present — because the lawsuit concerning the [uncertain: jewels] is not yet decided, and because the 9000 Rthl are registered on Szetlewek, so that he must be content with the interest, for the payment of which I have myself given an assurance. I shall do the same with the Ziemecki matter. Of Bernhardi's conduct I say nothing — for he was minded to treat me worse than the greatest usurer in the state, and by an eleven-day delay put me in the very greatest embarrassment — God be praised, I have concluded the business as happily as I could have imagined, and let the peasant run.

Should the Schlabrendorff woman be unmannerly, then everything here is provided for, and she would have every cause to repent a foolish conduct.

156 a)

Copy.

Your Serene Highness caused the Chancellor Hemuth to be assured, through the Councillor of War von Triebenfeld, in the most binding terms, that at the Christmas now past I should quite infallibly receive the arrears of the settlement monies for my children.

In full reliance upon the word [uncertain: given] me by Your [text lost], I have already disposed of this sum, payable these two years past, and [uncertain: beg] find myself now in the embarrassment of not being able to keep my own word.

By any further forbearance I should make myself answerable to my own children, and there remains to me therefore nothing but to have the suit in Berlin continued, if payment should not follow by the next post day.

Of this I most respectfully inform Your [Serene Highness] herewith, and have the honour, etc.

Wrocław, 16th Jan.

1805.

Countess von Schlabrendorff

Of the assistance of General von Köckritz I have not yet wished to make any use, because Amelang thinks to get through without it.

The [illegible] General commends himself most respectfully to Your Serene Highness.

The free pass for 120 [uncertain: buckets] of wine Your Serene Highness will doubtless already have there. In deepest reverence submission I remain Your Serene Highness's. I hear this very moment that Bernhardi has played another knavish trick. text_english:
156

Most Serene Prince,

Most gracious Lord!

If I had been able in any way whatever to obtain the 25000 Rthl without making the great transaction, I should long since have brought it about with the most glowing zeal.

But if I take the lesser sum, it costs, and my hands are tied, because I must pledge the heavy papers for the small loans just as much as for the large ones. As yet I have no first assurance [uncertain: when] I am to receive the capitals. The papers are found good and the security sufficient, but there is delay, God knows why.

I am certainly doing everything of which human powers are capable, and neither rest nor repose, [uncertain: in order] to reach the goal of all wishes. Only here nothing can be forced. Twice already we believed we had the money for certain, but an evil man has thwarted it; as I think,

it is young Eysenhardt — who claims to have 18000 Rthl to demand of Your Serene Highness as well; for these the Court Councillor Meyer will offer him the 20000 Rthl and take over the debt — I have declined this for the present — because the lawsuit concerning the [uncertain: jewels] is not yet decided, and because the 9000 Rthl are registered on Szetlewek, so that he must be content with the interest, for the payment of which I have myself given an assurance. I shall do the same with the Ziemecki matter. Of Bernhardi's conduct I say nothing — for he was minded to treat me worse than the greatest usurer in the state, and by an eleven-day delay put me in the very greatest embarrassment — God be praised, I have concluded the business as happily as I could have imagined, and let the peasant run.

Should the Schlabrendorff woman be unmannerly, then everything here is provided for, and she would have every cause to repent a foolish conduct.

156 a)

Copy.

Your Serene Highness caused the Chancellor Hemuth to be assured, through the Councillor of War von Triebenfeld, in the most binding terms, that at the Christmas now past I should quite infallibly receive the arrears of the settlement monies for my children.

In full reliance upon the word [uncertain: given] me by Your [text lost], I have already disposed of this sum, payable these two years past, and [uncertain: beg] find myself now in the embarrassment of not being able to keep my own word.

By any further forbearance I should make myself answerable to my own children, and there remains to me therefore nothing but to have the suit in Berlin continued, if payment should not follow by the next post day.

Of this I most respectfully inform Your [Serene Highness] herewith, and have the honour, etc.

Wrocław, 16th Jan.

1805.

Countess von Schlabrendorff

summary_en: Triebenfeld reports that he cannot obtain the 25000 Rthl without the large transaction. He says the money has twice been thwarted, probably by young Eysenhardt, who is demanding 18000 Rthl. He declined, for the time being, an offer from Court Councillor Meyer, since 9000 Rthl are entered against Szetlewek. Enclosed is a Copy in which Countess Schlabrendorff threatens to continue the suit in Berlin if the outstanding settlement money for her children is not paid by the next post day.
summary_de: Triebenfeld berichtet, dass er die 25000 Rthl ohne das große Geschäft nicht erhalten kann. Zweimal sei das Geld hintertrieben worden, vermutlich vom jungen Eysenhardt, der 18000 Rthl fordert. Ein Angebot des Hoffrath Meyer lehnte er vorerst ab, da 9000 Rthl auf Szetlewek eingetragen seien. Beigelegt ist eine Abschrift, in der Gräfin Schlabrendorff mit Fortsetzung der Klage in Berlin droht, falls die rückständigen Vergleichsgelder für ihre Kinder nicht bis zum nächsten Posttag gezahlt werden.

reading.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Berlin to the Prince. He has not been able to raise the 25000 rt without the "große Geschäft". The papers are judged good but the lenders hesitate. He thinks young Eysenhardt, who claims 18000 rt, has twice spoiled the deal. He has turned down for now an offer by Hoffrath Meyer (20000 rt, taking over the debt): the lawsuit is still open, and 9000 rthl are registered on Szetlewek. He complains of Bernhardi. Enclosure 156a is a copy of Gräfin Schlabrendorff's letter (Breslau, 16 Jan) threatening to continue her suit. Postscripts cover Köckritz and Amelang, a free pass for wine, and a new trick by Bernhardi.
